reading_comparisons.designer_translation:
Then two peoples, the Picts from the north and the Scots from the west, began to attack them, take their possessions and plunder; and they oppressed and humbled them for many years. Then, in that unrest, they sent messengers to Rome with letters and a weeping petition. They asked them for help and promised them humble obedience and constant submission if they helped them so that they might overcome their enemies. Then they sent them a large army for support; and as soon as they came onto this island they fought against their enemies, inflicted great slaughter on them, and drove and expelled them from their borders. They instructed them to build a fortification for their protection against their enemies; and so they went home with great victory.

When the former adversaries then perceived this, that the Roman army had gone away, they soon came with a fleet onto their frontiers, struck down and killed all whom they encountered, trampled them like ripe crops and destroyed them, and utterly oppressed them.
reading_comparisons.source_editor_translation:
Then two peoples, the Picts from the north and the Scots from the west, began to attack them, to take their possessions and to plunder; and for many years they afflicted and oppressed them. Then, amid that unrest, they sent messengers to Rome with letters and a tearful appeal: they asked them for help, and promised them humble obedience and continual subjection if they would help them so that they might overcome their enemies. Then they sent them a great army as help, and as soon as they came to this island they fought against their enemies, inflicted great slaughter on them, and drove and put them to flight out of their borders. They advised them to build a fortification for their protection against their enemies; and thus they went home with great victory.

When the former enemies then realized this—that the Roman army had gone away—they immediately came with a fleet into their territory, and struck down and killed all that they encountered, and trampled and destroyed them like ripe crops, and utterly ruined them.
reading_comparisons.decision: Both independent translations preserve the complete event chain, changing actors, prior Roman departure and final crop simile. Accept all they encountered as well as the contextual all whom; no human-only parsing is compulsory. Ordinary oppression/ruin synonyms remain defensible.

reading_comparisons.designer_translation: The man had built one house. Then his son came, and the son saw the house. The father said, “Now I have built the house.” The son said that he intended to travel. When the son departed, the father sat in the house. Then the son came, and he gave his father food.
reading_comparisons.source_editor_translation: The man had built a house. Then his son came, and the son saw the house. The father said, “Now I have built the house.” The son said that he intended to travel. When the son departed, the father then sat in the house. Then the son came, and he gave his father food.
reading_comparisons.decision: Both independently recover the completed building before arrival, direct speech, intended travel, asserted departure and food-giving return. The selected key keeps one house to make the assigned cardinal ān explicit; natural English a house does not by itself teach a new Old English article sense.
